property_summary: Only addresses marked as admin can successfully call newEmergencyOracle (call must NOT revert) — non-admin callers always revert.
Calls to newEmergencyOracle revert exactly when msg.sender is not an admin (i.e., only admin addresses can successfully call it).
newEmergencyOracle reverts iff the caller is not an admin (i.e., only admins can successfully call it).
Calling newEmergencyOracle should revert for callers who are NOT admins and succeed for callers who ARE admins (i.e., reverted == !isAdmin[msg.sender]).

When an admin calls newEmergencyOracle(description) the newly deployed EmergencyOracle contract's owner must equal the caller (msg.sender); the mutant that passes address(this) as owner causes the new oracle's owner to be the C contract address instead of the caller for some inputs.

For any admin caller address A and description D, after A calls newEmergencyOracle(D) the newly created EmergencyOracle's owner equals A in the reference, while the mutant that uses address(this) sets the owner to the contract address and thus can differ (detectable by reading the created oracle's owner via its public getter).

For any admin address and description, when that admin calls newEmergencyOracle(description) the created EmergencyOracle's owner should equal the caller (msg.sender) in the reference; the mutant that passes address(this) as owner breaks this by setting the new oracle's owner to the C contract address for some inputs.

For any admin caller address and any description, when that admin calls newEmergencyOracle(description) the reference contract deploys a new EmergencyOracle whose owner is equal to the msg.sender (the admin) — the mutant that passes address(this) instead sets the new oracle's owner to the C contract address for some admin addresses, so there exists an admin address input for which the created oracle's owner != caller.

For every call to newEmergencyOracle by an admin, the reference C deploys the EmergencyOracle such that the owner recorded in the deployed EmergencyOracle is equal to the admin caller (msg.sender); the mutant that passes address(this) as owner causes the deployed oracle's owner to be the C contract address for some admin callers, violating this property.

For any caller who is an admin, when newEmergencyOracle(description) is called the emitted NewEmergencyOracle event's first indexed owner argument equals the msg.sender (the admin); the mutant emits the new oracle address instead, breaking that equality for some inputs.

For any admin caller, C.newEmergencyOracle emits NewEmergencyOracle with the first indexed argument equal to the caller (msg.sender); the mutant emits the new oracle address instead, so this equality can be violated.

For any admin caller and any description string, the NewEmergencyOracle event's first indexed owner argument equals the caller (msg.sender); the mutant emits the new oracle address instead, violating this for descriptions that make the emitted newOracle distinct from the caller.

For any admin caller and any description, the reference contract always emits NewEmergencyOracle with the first argument equal to the caller (msg.sender); the mutant sometimes emits a different address (newOracle) breaking this invariant — we test this by calling newEmergencyOracle from a fuzzed admin address and then reading the emitted event owner via a newEmergencyOracle-created oracle's owner getter to detect mismatch.

For any admin caller and any description, the reference emits NewEmergencyOracle with the first indexed argument equal to the caller (msg.sender) so the newly deployed EmergencyOracle.owner() equals the original caller; the mutant emits the caller as newOracle instead, causing the deployed EmergencyOracle.owner() to differ from the logged owner for some inputs.

For any admin caller and any description, after newEmergencyOracle(...) returns the newly created oracle address must NOT be an admin (isAdmin[newOracle] == false); the mutant sets isAdmin[newOracle]=true and thus violates this rule for some inputs.

For every admin caller and any description, when newEmergencyOracle(...) returns the created oracle address must not be marked admin (isAdmin[newOracle] == false); the mutant assigns isAdmin[newOracle]=true which violates this rule for some inputs.

For every admin caller and any description, the newly created EmergencyOracle contract address is not recorded as an admin in c.isAdmin (reference preserves isAdmin[newOracle] == false for all inputs; the mutant sets isAdmin[newOracle] = true and thus breaks this invariant for some input).
